headline: Kai, the S&P ended a jobs-shock week at a record close, and Tehran now calls the Hormuz framework final.
subline: Rate-hike odds faded to 44%, gold and the Nasdaq had big weeks, and CPI lands Wednesday.
asof: Weekend edition · indexes, yield and Brent are Friday's close; gold is Friday morning's futures print; bitcoin as of ~6:40 AM ET Saturday · every figure links to its source below

items.title: Payrolls fall 23,000; S&P closes at record
items.sentence: July payrolls fell 23,000 against forecasts of an 80,000 gain, September rate-hike odds slid to 44%, and the S&P 500 rose 0.62% to a record 7,757.64, per Reuters.

items.title: Ten-year yield eases to 4.65%
items.sentence: The 10-year slipped 4 basis points to 4.65% — still above its 12-month average of 4.27% — with the 2-year at 4.19% and the 30-year at 5.19%, per Forbes Advisor.

items.title: Atlassian jumps 36% on cloud acceleration
items.sentence: Fourth-quarter revenue grew 28% with cloud up 31%, margins widened sharply, and CEO Mike Cannon-Brookes said he will buy up to $250 million of stock, per Yahoo Finance.

items.title: Gold prints new records into the weekend
items.sentence: December futures opened flat at $4,298.30 and ran to $4,411.70 by Friday morning — up 4.8% in a week and 27% in a year — per Yahoo Finance.

items.title: Brent settles at $83.55 after a jumpy week
items.sentence: Brent rose 1.29% to $83.55 a barrel Friday, per Trading Economics, capping a week in which Hormuz escalation built a premium that deal optimism then trimmed.

items.title: Bitcoin firms near $65,000 on ETF inflows
items.sentence: Bitcoin trades around $64,984, up about 1.3% in 24 hours, with spot-ETF inflows back and wallets holding 10 to 10,000 BTC adding more than 20,000 coins since late July, per The Sunday Guardian.

items.title: Tehran says Hormuz framework is finalized
items.sentence: Iranian official Hassan Ghashghavi said the general framework of the Oman agreement is done — a 60-day interim shipping regime for the strait — while Washington insists on no tolls, per ABC News.

items.title: Spain's Ceuta reels after viral border rush
items.sentence: Nearly 60,000 people converged on the enclave after a court ruling spread online as an open door, at least 67 people drowned, and Spain declared a state of emergency, per Al Jazeera.

items.title: Ukraine strikes refineries 700 km inside Russia
items.sentence: Kyiv hit refineries in Bashkortostan and Yaroslavl, while Russian strikes killed two at a Kharkiv rail station and one aboard a grain ship, per Euronews.

items.title: Trump moves again on birthright citizenship
items.sentence: The president signed two executive orders attempting to limit birthright citizenship after a Supreme Court rejection, per Jacob Redman's Everything Briefing.

items.title: White House finalizes frontier-model framework
items.sentence: About a dozen firms including Anthropic, OpenAI, Google and Meta agreed to give Washington access to frontier models 30 days before release, with no plans to publish the text, per NY1.

items.title: Anthropic signs $10 billion compute deal with Volta
items.sentence: The six-year agreement puts Anthropic capacity on a week-old a16z-backed cloud valued at $2.4 billion, running from Bitdeer's Norway facility, per Carly's AI news roundup.

items.title: Apple names 11 more ex-staff in OpenAI suit
items.sentence: Apple's preliminary-injunction motion says the former employees may have kept confidential data before joining OpenAI, with a hearing set for October 1, per Carly's AI news roundup.

items.title: Google consolidates AI leadership in California
items.sentence: Bloomberg reports Google is shifting AI power to California as it races Anthropic and OpenAI.

items.title: SpaceX rallies 15.8% as lockup expires
items.sentence: Shares gained 15.8% after a post-listing share lockup expired, one of Friday's standout moves, per Reuters.
